name: Content first
summary: Large, calm type and generous space, for people who come to read.
description: Content first is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Large, calm type and generous space, for people who come to read.

ai.use_when: Publications, documentation, blogs, guides and help centers.
ai.avoid_when: Data-heavy tools or screens with many actions.

scenarios: A reader arrives from search on a phone and reads a long guide in one sitting.
A returning reader saves an article to finish on the train.

voice.summary: Conversational and warm. Talk to one reader, like a good editor would.
principles: Short sentences with room to breathe.
Explain why before asking for anything.

tone.error: Calm and helpful. Take the blame, offer the way forward.
tone.empty: An invitation, not a dead end.
tone.confirm: Gentle and clear about what changes.
tone.onboarding: One sentence on what is here and why it is worth reading.

examples.text: We could not save your email. Check it and try again.
You're in. The next issue arrives on Friday.
Nothing saved yet. Tap Save on any article to read it later.
Unsubscribe from the weekly letter? You can come back any time.

answers.question: business.q1
answers.why: The product publishes articles and guides.

answers.question: business.q2
answers.why: One publication, one brand.

answers.question: people.q1
answers.why: Most readers arrive from search and visit now and then.

answers.question: people.q2
answers.why: AA is the commitment for a public site.

answers.question: content.q1
answers.why: The content is long-form text.

answers.question: content.q2
answers.why: One idea per screen keeps reading calm.

answers.question: tasks.q1
answers.why: People read from start to end.

answers.question: tasks.q2
answers.why: Actions are rare: subscribe, share, save.

answers.question: human.q1
answers.why: Attention belongs to the text.

answers.question: human.q2
answers.why: Visitors see the interface fresh each time.

answers.question: outcomes.q1
answers.why: Comfortable reading is the measure.

answers.question: outcomes.q2
answers.why: Losing your place in an article breaks the read.

answers.question: brand.q1
answers.why: Warm and considered, like a good magazine.

answers.question: brand.q2
answers.why: The brand shows in type, not in color.

answers.question: voice.q1
answers.why: The voice talks to one reader.

answers.question: voice.q2
answers.why: Neutral formality suits every topic.

answers.question: team.q1
answers.why: A small editorial team.

answers.question: team.q2
answers.why: The design changes rarely.

answers.question: typography.q1
answers.why: A lead and a display role open articles.

answers.question: typography.q2
answers.why: Large body text is easy on the eyes.

answers.question: typography.q3
answers.why: Line height is a ratio, so it grows with the text.

answers.question: color.q1
answers.why: Primary, secondary and a text link.

answers.question: color.q2
answers.why: Status is rare; color and a word are enough.

answers.question: color.q3
answers.why: A calm, balanced palette.

answers.question: spacing.q1
answers.why: Room around the text helps reading.

answers.question: spacing.q2
answers.why: One density everywhere.

answers.question: spacing.q3
answers.why: Space separates sections; lines add noise.

answers.question: shape.q1
answers.why: Rounded corners feel friendly.

answers.question: shape.q2
answers.why: Regular borders read clearly on warm paper.

answers.question: shape.q3
answers.why: Pills feel softer next to text.

answers.question: elevation.q1
answers.why: Only menus and dialogs float.

answers.question: elevation.q2
answers.why: Soft shadows match the warm brand.

answers.question: elevation.q3
answers.why: Dimming focuses the reader on the dialog.

answers.question: motion.q1
answers.why: Motion guides from one part to the next.

answers.question: motion.q2
answers.why: Moderate speed feels calm.

answers.question: motion.q3
answers.why: When asked, nothing moves.

answers.question: iconography.q1
answers.why: Occasional visitors need a word next to each icon.

answers.question: iconography.q2
answers.why: Outline icons stay quiet next to text.

answers.question: iconography.q3
answers.why: Icons match the text size.

answers.question: theming.q1
answers.why: Light and dark ship as standard for night readers.

answers.question: theming.q2
answers.why: One publication, one brand.

answers.question: theming.q3
answers.why: Readers pick light or dark.

answers.question: accessibility.q1
answers.why: AA contrast for all text.

answers.question: accessibility.q2
answers.why: Many readers are on phones.

answers.question: accessibility.q3
answers.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.

answers.question: naming.q1
answers.why: Role names survive a redesign.

answers.question: naming.q2
answers.why: Primitives, semantics and component keys.

answers.question: naming.q3
answers.why: A component API keeps changes local.

usage.why: Display is kept for the landing moment; article titles stay calm.
Tables are rare and read row by row.

usage.use: type.body, at most 65 characters a line
usage.why: A large size and short lines make long text easy on the eyes.
Caption is too faint for a label people must read.
A tint shows the choice clearly on warm paper.
The sentence says what to fix; color only draws the eye.
Readers expect links to be underlined inside text.
Status is rare; a word is clear.
Text needs air even inside a group.
Space alone separates sections; lines add noise.
Rows are read, not scanned.
Rounded corners feel friendly.
Pills sit softly next to text.
Cards stay flat on the page; shadows are for floating things.
The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.
Moderate speed feels calm.
When people ask for less motion, nothing moves.

usage.use: Not used: always add a word
usage.why: Occasional visitors do not know icons.
Only semantic colors change; the reading layout stays.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.
Many readers are on phones.
One clear action per section.

usage.use: Button ghost as a text link
usage.why: A link feels lighter and does not compete.

usage.use: Button secondary with the full verb, then confirm
usage.why: Naming the verb and confirming prevents a mistake.
Occasional visitors need the word.

color.$description: The color options. Semantics pick from these; components never read them.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.
Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

fast.$description: Fast: the usual convention for feedback, about 120ms.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower, springy speed for expressive motion, about 320ms.
